Story · Lesson 1

Omar Is Late

It is 7:50, and Omar is running. Read the story, then read it again from Omar's point of view.

Say what is happening nowAsk: What are you doing?Tell a story as it happens
7:50Omar is running
7:52a rickshaw is coming
7:58he is looking at his watch
8:00the door is closed
Friday!Adam is sleeping

1The story

It is 7:50 in the morning. Omar is running down the street. His bag is jumping on his back. He is late for class!

A rickshaw is coming. "Stop, please!" The driver is smiling. "Where are you going?" "To Future Vision Institute. Quickly, please!" Now the rickshaw is flying through the streets. Omar is looking at his watch. It is 7:58.

The rickshaw stops at the institute. Omar is paying the driver, and he is running to the door. But the door is closed. There are no students. It is very quiet.

Omar calls Adam. "Adam! Where are you? What are you doing?" Adam is in bed. "I'm sleeping, Omar. Today is Friday!"

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
What time is it?It's 7:50.
2
What is Omar doing?He's running down the street.
3
Is he late for class?Yes, he is.
4
What is coming?A rickshaw.
5
Is the driver smiling?Yes, he is.
6
Where is Omar going?To Future Vision Institute.
7
What is Omar looking at?His watch.
8
Is the door of the institute open?No, it isn't. It's closed.
9
Are there students there?No, there aren't.
10
Who does Omar call?Adam.
11
What is Adam doing?He's sleeping.
12
Why is the institute closed?Because today is Friday!

3Point of view Now Omar tells the story.

O

It's 7:50 in the morning. I'm running down the street. My bag is jumping on my back. I'm late for class!

A rickshaw is coming. "Stop, please!" The driver is smiling. "Where are you going?" "To Future Vision Institute. Quickly, please!" Now we are flying through the streets. I'm looking at my watch. It's 7:58.

The rickshaw stops at the institute. I'm paying the driver, and I'm running to the door. But the door is closed. There are no students.

I call Adam. "Adam! What are you doing?" "I'm sleeping, Omar. Today is Friday!"

4What did you learn?

You learned the present continuous.

We use it for things that are happening now, at this moment.

Ihe · she · ityou · we · they
I am running.He is running.We are running.
I'm not sleeping.She isn't sleeping.They aren't sleeping.
Am I late?Is he smiling?What are you doing?
be + verb + -ingHe is running. They are sleeping.
Now, at this momentLook! A rickshaw is coming.
run → running · smile → smilingSome verbs double the last letter. Others lose the e.
QuestionsWhat are you doing?I'm reading. / I'm studying.

5New words

lateafter the right time
rickshawa small taxi with three wheels
drivera person who drives a car or a bus
quicklyfast
watcha small clock you wear on your arm
closednot open

Topic · Lesson 2

Getting Around

Buses, minibuses, rickshaws and taxis, and a busy bus station.

Name ways to travelSay what is good about each oneDescribe a busy place

1Read

How do people get around in the city? Many people take the bus. Buses are cheap, but they are often full. A minibus is small and fast, and it stops when you ask.

A rickshaw has three wheels. It is great for short trips, and the driver can take you to the door. A taxi is more expensive, but it is comfortable.

Look at the bus station now. It is very busy. People are waiting for their buses, the drivers are calling "Market! Market!", and a man is selling cold water and juice.

2Ways to get around

busbig · cheap · often full
minibussmall · fast
rickshawthree wheels · short trips
taxiexpensive · comfortable

3Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Are buses cheap or expensive?Cheap. But they are often full.
2
When does a minibus stop?When you ask.
3
How many wheels does a rickshaw have?Three.
4
Is a taxi cheap?No, it isn't. It's more expensive.
5
Is the bus station busy now?Yes, it is. It's very busy.
6
What is the man selling?Cold water and juice.

4New words

get aroundgo from place to place
cheapnot expensive
fullwith no more space
wheelsthe round parts that turn under a car
tripsa trip is a short journey: home, work, the market
comfortablenice and easy to sit in

Conversation · Lesson 3

Which Bus Goes to the Market?

At the bus station, asking the way and the fare

Ask which bus to takeAsk the fareAsk how long a trip takes

1Read the conversation

Sara is at the bus station. She wants to go to the big market.
SSARAExcuse me. Is this bus going to the market?
DDRIVERNo, it isn't. This bus is going to the hospital.
SSARAOh. Which bus goes to the market?
DDRIVERThe green bus. Look, it's coming now!
SSARAThank you! How much is it?
DDRIVERFive hundred pounds.
SSARAAnd how long does it take?
DDRIVERAbout twenty minutes.
SSARAGreat. Thanks for your help!
DDRIVERYou're welcome.

2Useful phrases

Start politely

Excuse me.

Check the bus

Is this bus going to the market?
— No, it isn't.

Ask which one

Which bus goes to the market?
— The green bus.

Ask the fare

How much is it?
— Five hundred pounds.

Ask the time

How long does it take?
— About twenty minutes.

Say thank you

Thanks for your help!
— You're welcome.

3New words

whichwhat one of two or more
how longhow much time
takehere: need (time). It takes twenty minutes.
helpwhat you do to make things easy for someone

Story · Lesson 4

Where Were You, Adam?

Adam was not in class yesterday. Read the story in the past, then read it again as it happens today.

Talk about yesterdayAsk: Where were you?Say where you were

1The story

Yesterday was Monday. Sara and Omar were in class, but Adam wasn't there. His chair was empty. Mr. Ali was surprised, because Adam is never absent.

In the evening, Omar was on the phone with Adam. "Where were you today, Adam? Were you sick?" "No, I wasn't. I was at the hospital with my grandfather. He was sick."

"Oh no! Was it bad?" "Yes, it was. We were at the hospital all day. My mother and my uncle were there, too. The doctors were very kind."

Today Adam is back in class. His grandfather is at home now, and he is OK. "Welcome back, Adam!" Sara and Omar are happy, and Mr. Ali is happy, too.

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Was yesterday Monday?Yes, it was.
2
Were Sara and Omar in class?Yes, they were.
3
Was Adam in class?No, he wasn't.
4
Was his chair empty?Yes, it was.
5
Was Mr. Ali surprised or happy?Surprised. Adam is never absent.
6
Where was Omar in the evening?On the phone with Adam.
7
Was Adam sick?No, he wasn't.
8
Where was Adam?At the hospital.
9
Who was sick?His grandfather.
10
Were they at the hospital all day?Yes, they were.
11
Were the doctors kind?Yes, they were. They were very kind.
12
Where is his grandfather now?At home. He's OK now.

3Point of view Now the same story happens today.

O

Today is Monday. Sara and I are in class, but Adam isn't here. His chair is empty. Mr. Ali is surprised, because Adam is never absent.

In the evening, I'm on the phone with Adam. "Where are you, Adam? Are you sick?" "No, I'm not. I'm at the hospital with my grandfather. He is sick."

"Oh no! Is it bad?" "Yes, it is. We are here all day. My mother and my uncle are here, too. The doctors are very kind."

4What did you learn?

You learned was and were.

They are the past of am, is and are. We use them for yesterday, last week, and other times before now.

NowBefore now
I am at home. · He is sick.I was at home. · He was sick.
We are at the hospital.We were at the hospital.
He isn't here. · They aren't here.He wasn't here. · They weren't here.
Is it bad? · Are you sick?Was it bad? · Were you sick?
I · he · she · it → wasI was at home. It was bad.
you · we · they → wereWe were at the hospital all day.
Not: wasn't · weren'tAdam wasn't in class. They weren't at home.
QuestionsWere you in class yesterday?Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.

5New words

yesterdaythe day before today
emptywith nothing and no one in it
surprisedfeeling that something is not what you expected
absentnot here; not at school or work
all dayfrom morning to evening
backhere again

Topic · Lesson 5

The Weather in Sudan

Three seasons, and what the weather was like yesterday.

Name the seasonsDescribe the weatherSay what the weather was like

1Read

Sudan is a hot country. The summer is from April to June. It is very hot, often more than forty degrees.

The rainy season is from July to September. There are big storms, and the Nile is high. The winter is from December to February. It is not cold, but the mornings are cool and nice.

What was the weather like yesterday? In Khartoum, it was sunny and very hot. In Port Sudan, it was hot and humid. There were no clouds in the sky.

2Three seasons

summerApril to June · very hot
rainy seasonJuly to September · storms
winterDecember to February · cool mornings

3Weather words

sunnya lot of sun
cloudya lot of clouds
rainyrain is falling
windya lot of wind
humidhot and wet air
coola little cold

4Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
When is the summer in Sudan?From April to June.
2
Is the summer hot?Yes, it is. It's very hot.
3
When is the rainy season?From July to September.
4
Is the winter cold?No, it isn't. But the mornings are cool.
5
What was the weather like in Khartoum yesterday?It was sunny and very hot.
6
Were there clouds in the sky?No, there weren't.

5New words

weatherhow hot, cold, rainy, or windy it is
countrya land with its own people, like Sudan or Egypt
degreeswe measure heat in degrees: 40 degrees is very hot
seasona part of the year: summer, winter
stormsstrong wind and rain
skythe space above us, where the sun is

How Was Your Weekend?

Talking with a friend about the weekend

Ask about the weekendSay where you wereReact to news

1Read the conversation

On Sunday morning, Sara and Adam talk before class.
SSARAGood morning, Adam! How was your weekend?
AADAMIt was great, thanks. I was at my uncle's farm.
SSARAA farm? Where is it?
AADAMIt's near the Nile, about an hour from the city.
SSARAWere there animals?
AADAMYes, there were cows, goats, and a lot of chickens! And you?
SSARAIt was busy! My cousin's wedding was on Friday.
AADAMWow! Was it big?
SSARAVery big. There were three hundred people, and the music was great.
AADAMThat sounds fun!

2Useful phrases

Ask about the weekend

How was your weekend?
— It was great, thanks.

Say where you were

I was at my uncle's farm.

Ask about it

Were there animals?
— Yes, there were.

Ask back

And you?

Describe it

It was busy. · It was quiet.

React

Wow! · That sounds fun!

3New words

farmland where people grow food and keep animals
cousinthe child of your uncle or aunt
weddingthe day two people get married
soundsseems, from what you hear: That sounds fun!

Story · Lesson 7

The Big Match

Omar's first match with Adam's team. Read the story, then read it again from Omar's point of view.

Tell what happenedUse past verbsTalk about a game

1The story

Last Friday, Adam's team played a big match against the Blue Stars. Omar played, too. It was his first match with the team.

The match started at five o'clock. The Blue Stars were very good. After ten minutes, they scored a goal. Then they scored again. At half time, the coach talked to the team. "Don't stop. You can win!"

In the second half, Adam ran fast and scored a goal. Then Omar got the ball and scored, too. Two–two! Everybody jumped and shouted.

One minute before the end, Omar saw the ball near the goal. He kicked it very hard, and goal! Adam's team won, three–two. After the match, they went to a café and had tea and cake. Omar was the star of the day.

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Who played a big match last Friday?Adam's team.
2
Who was the other team?The Blue Stars.
3
Was it Omar's first match with the team?Yes, it was.
4
What time was the match?At five o'clock.
5
Who scored first?The Blue Stars.
6
Who talked to the team at half time?The coach.
7
Who scored the first goal for Adam's team?Adam.
8
Who scored next?Omar.
9
Who jumped and shouted?Everybody.
10
Who scored the last goal?Omar!
11
Who won?Adam's team, three–two.
12
Where were they after the match?At a café. They had tea and cake.

3Point of view Now Omar tells the story.

O

Last Friday, my team played a big match against the Blue Stars. It was my first match with the team.

The match started at five o'clock. The Blue Stars were very good. After ten minutes, they scored a goal. Then they scored again. At half time, the coach talked to us. "Don't stop. You can win!"

In the second half, Adam ran fast and scored a goal. Then I got the ball and scored, too. Two–two! Everybody jumped and shouted.

One minute before the end, I saw the ball near the goal. I kicked it very hard, and goal! We won, three–two. After the match, we went to a café and had tea and cake. What a day!

4What did you learn?

You learned the past simple.

We use it for things that happened and finished before now, like yesterday or last Friday.

Most verbs: add -edSome verbs change
play → played · start → startedrun → ran · get → got
talk → talked · kick → kickedsee → saw · win → won
score → scored · smile → smiledgo → went · have → had
The same for everyoneI played, he played, they played.
Ends in -e: add only -dscore → scored, smile → smiled
Learn the verbs that changego → went, have → had, see → saw
QuestionsWho scored the last goal?Omar scored it!

5New words

teama group of players who play together
matcha game between two teams
againston the other side in a game
goala point in football
coachthe person who trains a team
half timethe short stop in the middle of a match

Topic · Lesson 8

On My Phone

Messages, photos, groups and social media, and what we did online yesterday.

Talk about your phoneUse words for social mediaSay what you did online

1Read

Today, almost everyone has a phone. We send messages to our friends and family, we make calls, and we take photos and videos.

Many people use social media. We chat in groups with our class or our family, and we share news, photos, and videos.

Yesterday, Sara posted a photo of her cousin's wedding. Her friends liked it, and many people wrote nice comments. Omar sent a voice message to Adam: "Great match on Friday!"

But be careful. Never share your password, and don't stay on your phone all night!

2Phone words

messagewords you send on the phone
postput a photo or words online
sharesend to other people
likeshow that you enjoy a post
commentwords under a post
passworda secret word for your phone or app

3Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Does almost everyone have a phone today?Yes, they do.
2
What do we share in groups?News, photos, and videos.
3
What was in Sara's photo?Her cousin's wedding.
4
Who liked Sara's photo?Her friends.
5
Who sent a voice message?Omar.
6
Is it OK to share your password?No, it isn't. Never share it.

4New words

almostnearly; not all but very close
videosmoving pictures you make with a phone or camera
newsnew information about something
voicethe sound you make when you speak
carefulthinking about what you do so nothing bad happens
nevernot at any time

Story · Lesson 10

Did Omar Cook Fish?

Last level, Omar said "Next week, fish!" Did he do it? Read the story, then read it again from Omar's point of view.

Say what you didn't doAsk: Did you…?Answer: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

1The story

Last week, Omar wanted to cook fish. He went to the market and bought a big fish. But he didn't know how to cook it, and he didn't call his mother. "I can do it," he said.

He didn't clean the fish well, and he didn't use much oil. He put it in a hot pan and didn't watch it. He was on his phone!

Soon the kitchen was full of smoke. Adam came in. "Did you burn the fish?" "Yes, I did," Omar said. "Can we eat it?" "No, we can't!"

So they didn't eat fish. They ate sandwiches again. The next day, Omar called his mother. "Did you watch the pan?" she asked. "No, I didn't." She laughed. "Next time, put down your phone!"

2Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Did Omar want to cook fish?Yes, he did.
2
Did he buy a small fish?No, he didn't. He bought a big fish.
3
Did he know how to cook it?No, he didn't.
4
Did he call his mother?No, he didn't.
5
Did he use much oil?No, he didn't.
6
Did he watch the pan?No, he didn't. He was on his phone.
7
What was the kitchen full of?Smoke.
8
Who came in?Adam.
9
Did Omar burn the fish?Yes, he did.
10
Did they eat the fish?No, they didn't.
11
What did they eat?Sandwiches, again.
12
What did his mother say?"Next time, put down your phone!"

3Point of view Now Omar tells the story.

O

Last week, I wanted to cook fish. I went to the market and bought a big fish. But I didn't know how to cook it, and I didn't call my mother. "I can do it," I said.

I didn't clean the fish well, and I didn't use much oil. I put it in a hot pan and didn't watch it. I was on my phone!

Soon the kitchen was full of smoke. Adam came in. "Did you burn the fish?" "Yes, I did."

So we didn't eat fish. We ate sandwiches again. The next day, I called my mother. "Did you watch the pan?" "No, I didn't." She laughed. "Next time, put down your phone!"

4What did you learn?

You learned didn't and Did.

In the past simple, we say no with didn't and ask with Did. After them, the verb goes back to its first form.

PastNot · Questions
He bought a big fish.He didn't buy a small fish.
They ate sandwiches.They didn't eat fish.
He burned the fish.Did he burn the fish? Yes, he did.
She laughed.Did she laugh? Yes, she did.
didn't = did notWe usually say didn't.
After didn't and Did: the first formHe didn't eat. Not: didn't ate.
The same for everyoneI didn't, she didn't, they didn't.
QuestionsDid you cook yesterday?Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

5New words

boughtthe past of buy
oila yellow liquid we cook with
smokethe gray cloud that comes from fire
burncook too much
soonafter a short time
put downput something on a table or the floor

Topic · Lesson 11

My Grandfather's Photo

Describing people, then and now.

Describe peopleSay how people looked beforeCompare then and now

1Read

This is an old photo of Adam's grandfather. It is from 1975. In the photo, he was young and tall. He had black hair and a mustache. He was thin, and he had a big smile.

Now Adam's grandfather is seventy-five. He is not tall now, and his hair is white. He has a beard, and he wears glasses. But he still has the same big smile.

How do we describe people? We talk about their height (tall, short), their hair (black, white, curly, straight), their eyes (brown, black), and their age (young, old).

2Then and now

In 1975young · tall · black hair · a mustache
Nowseventy-five · white hair · a beard · glasses

3Words for people

tall↔ short
young↔ old
thin↔ heavy
curly hair↔ straight hair
a beardhair on the face and chin
glassesthey help you see

4Questions and answers Answer fast. Short answers are fine.

1
Is the photo old or new?Old. It's from 1975.
2
Was his grandfather tall in the photo?Yes, he was.
3
Did he have black hair?Yes, he did.
4
Did he have a beard in the photo?No, he didn't. He had a mustache.
5
Is his hair black now?No, it isn't. It's white.
6
Does he still have a big smile?Yes, he does.

5New words

mustachehair above the mouth
thinnot fat
wearshas something on his body: clothes, glasses
stillthe same as before
describesay what someone or something is like
agehow old you are

Conversation · Lesson 12

At the Pharmacy

Saying what is wrong and getting help

Say what is wrongAnswer questions about the pastUnderstand simple advice

1Read the conversation

Sara has a headache. After class, she goes to the pharmacy near the institute.
PPHARMACISTGood afternoon. Can I help you?
SSARAYes, please. I have a bad headache.
PPHARMACISTI'm sorry. When did it start?
SSARAIt started this morning.
PPHARMACISTDid you take anything?
SSARANo, I didn't.
PPHARMACISTDid you drink enough water today?
SSARANot really. It was very hot, and I was busy.
PPHARMACISTTake one of these pills now, and drink a lot of water. Feel better soon!
SSARAThank you very much!

2Useful phrases

Offer help

Can I help you?
— Yes, please.

Say what is wrong

I have a bad headache.

Ask when

When did it start?
— This morning.

Ask about medicine

Did you take anything?
— No, I didn't.

Give advice

Drink a lot of water.

Wish someone well

Feel better soon!
— Thank you!

3New words

headachea pain in your head
pharmacya shop that sells medicine
pillssmall pieces of medicine that you swallow
enoughas much as you need
